mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last two quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in the last month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL below 2% for 3 consecutive months) signals a stable monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors favor equities over fixed income.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% and consumer spending (RSAFS) increases by more than 2% in the same month, it signals a strong demand side of the economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and RSAFS increases > 2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in the last month, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2%, signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% for 3 consecutive months signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as liquidity flows into risk assets.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.
